chapters.title: What Is Astronomy?
chapters.tease: The oldest science still asks the biggest questions, using only the light and messengers that reach Earth.

chapters.title: The Celestial Sphere
chapters.tease: Picturing the sky as a globe gave every star a fixed address, so any telescope on Earth can find any object.

chapters.title: Constellations
chapters.tease: Eighty-eight agreed regions turned a sky of myths into a shared postcode system for every object.

chapters.title: Why the Sky Turns
chapters.tease: One spinning planet explains the rising, setting and wheeling of every star in the sky.

chapters.title: The Seasons
chapters.tease: A 23.4-degree lean, not our distance from the Sun, sets the rhythm of farming, migration and the ice ages.

chapters.title: Phases of the Moon
chapters.tease: The Moon's changing face gave humanity its first clock and the word month.

chapters.title: Eclipses
chapters.tease: Rare alignments of Sun, Moon and Earth revealed helium, confirmed relativity and still stop the world in its tracks.

chapters.title: Starlight & Magnitude
chapters.tease: A 2,000-year-old ranking of starlight became the yardstick for measuring energy across the universe.

chapters.title: Light-Years
chapters.tease: Because light takes time to travel, every telescope looks into the past.

chapters.title: Observing Without a Telescope
chapters.tease: Patience and darkness alone reveal thousands of stars, five planets and our own galaxy.

chapters.title: The First Astronomers
chapters.tease: Long before telescopes, stones, tablets and gears turned the sky into humanity's first clock and calendar.

chapters.title: Ptolemy's Universe
chapters.tease: A wrong model with Earth at the centre, yet it predicted the planets well enough to rule astronomy for 1,400 years.

chapters.title: The Copernican Turn
chapters.tease: Moving the Sun to the centre barely improved the maths but changed humanity's place in the cosmos.

chapters.title: Galileo's Telescope
chapters.tease: A spyglass sold to Venice for spotting ships became the instrument that showed Earth is not the centre.

chapters.title: Kepler's Laws
chapters.tease: Kepler used Tycho's data to replace perfect circles with ellipses, and found three laws that every orbit obeys.

chapters.title: Newton's Gravity
chapters.tease: One inverse-square law explained the apple, the tides, Kepler's orbits and the return of Halley's comet.

chapters.title: Herschel's Deep Sky
chapters.tease: A musician and his sister swept the sky from Bath, found a new planet and catalogued the deep universe.

chapters.title: The Great Debate
chapters.tease: Two astronomers argued over whether the spiral nebulae lay inside our galaxy. A flickering star settled it.

chapters.title: Hubble's Expanding Sky
chapters.tease: Hubble found that galaxies recede faster the farther away they are: the universe itself is expanding.

chapters.title: Astronomy Goes Multiband
chapters.tease: Visible light is one octave of a vast spectrum; radio, infrared, X-ray and gamma eyes revealed a hidden universe.

chapters.title: The Sun's Family
chapters.tease: One star holds 99.86% of the mass; eight planets, five dwarf planets and millions of small bodies share the rest.

chapters.title: Mercury
chapters.tease: The smallest planet spins three times every two orbits, and its odd orbit helped prove Einstein's theory of gravity.

chapters.title: Venus
chapters.tease: Earth's twin in size became the hottest planet, a living lesson in how a greenhouse effect can run away.

chapters.title: Earth & Moon
chapters.tease: A Mars-sized collision made the Moon, and the Moon now steadies our tilt, drives the tides and stretches our days.

chapters.title: Mars
chapters.tease: The tallest volcano and longest canyon we know sit on a desert world that once had rivers and lakes.

chapters.title: The Asteroid Belt
chapters.tease: Jupiter's pull kept a planet from forming, leaving an archive of the solar system's first building blocks.

chapters.title: Jupiter
chapters.tease: The largest planet stirs comets, powers the solar system's biggest magnetic field and holds oceans in its moons.

chapters.title: Saturn's Rings
chapters.tease: A 280,000 km wide disc only about 10 metres thick, made of ice, sculpted by moons and slowly raining away.

chapters.title: The Ice Giants
chapters.tease: Two blue worlds, one found by chance and one by mathematics, visited only once and still barely understood.

chapters.title: Pluto & the Kuiper Belt
chapters.tease: Pluto opened a third zone of the solar system, a frozen frontier that stretches thousands of times farther than Neptune.

chapters.title: Anatomy of the Sun
chapters.tease: Every joule of daylight was forged in a core the size of a few hundred Earths, then took millennia to escape.

chapters.title: Nuclear Fusion
chapters.tease: One reaction, hydrogen into helium, lights every star and explains where sunlight comes from.

chapters.title: Space Weather
chapters.tease: The Sun's magnetic moods can light the sky with auroras or knock out power grids and satellites.

chapters.title: Stellar Nurseries
chapters.tease: Every star, the Sun included, began as a cold dark cloud that gravity pulled into a furnace.

chapters.title: The Main Sequence
chapters.tease: Mass alone sets how bright a star shines and how long it lives, from a few million years to trillions.

chapters.title: The HR Diagram
chapters.tease: One chart of colour against brightness sorted the stars and revealed how they live and age.

chapters.title: Red Giants & White Dwarfs
chapters.tease: The Sun's own future, and the fate of 97 per cent of stars, is a gentle swelling and a long cooling.

chapters.title: Supernovae
chapters.tease: Exploding stars scatter the oxygen, calcium and iron of which planets and people are made.

chapters.title: Neutron Stars & Pulsars
chapters.tease: City-sized stellar corpses that spin like lighthouses became the most precise clocks in nature.

chapters.title: Black Holes
chapters.tease: Once a mathematical oddity, black holes are now weighed, heard and photographed, testing gravity itself.

chapters.title: The Milky Way
chapters.tease: Mapping our own galaxy from inside showed that the Sun is an ordinary star in an ordinary suburb.

chapters.title: Galaxy Types
chapters.tease: Sorting galaxies by shape showed that their forms record histories of quiet growth or violent mergers.

chapters.title: Andromeda
chapters.tease: Hubble's 1923 Cepheid in Andromeda proved the universe is full of galaxies, not just one.

chapters.title: Galaxy Mergers
chapters.tease: Mergers build big galaxies, light starbursts and feed black holes: the main way galaxies grow.

chapters.title: Supermassive Black Holes
chapters.tease: Every big galaxy hides a black hole of millions to billions of Suns that shapes how its galaxy grows.

chapters.title: Quasars
chapters.tease: Quasars revealed that feeding black holes are the most efficient power sources in the universe.

chapters.title: Dark Matter's Grip
chapters.tease: Flat rotation curves showed that every galaxy is held together by far more matter than we can see.

chapters.title: Galaxy Clusters
chapters.tease: Clusters, the largest settled objects, weigh dark matter, act as natural telescopes and test dark energy.

chapters.title: The Local Group
chapters.tease: Our gravitationally bound home: two giants, Triangulum and over a hundred dwarfs that will never drift apart.

chapters.title: The Cosmic Web
chapters.tease: Mapping the cosmic web showed that gravity has spun the Big Bang's ripples into a universe-wide foam.

chapters.title: The Big Bang
chapters.tease: It gave the universe a history: a beginning, a recipe and an age measured to a fraction of a per cent.

chapters.title: The Cosmic Afterglow
chapters.tease: The oldest light in the universe is a baby photograph that fixed its age, shape and ingredients.

chapters.title: The Expanding Universe
chapters.tease: It showed the universe has a history: rewind the stretching and everything meets in a hot, dense beginning.

chapters.title: Redshift
chapters.tease: One number from a spectrum tells how far away a galaxy is and how long ago its light set out.

chapters.title: Dark Energy
chapters.tease: Finding that expansion is speeding up revealed that two-thirds of the universe is something nobody understands.

chapters.title: Inflation
chapters.tease: It explains why the universe is smooth and flat, and how quantum noise became the seeds of galaxies.

chapters.title: Making the Elements
chapters.tease: It traced every element to its forge, showing that the matter in our bodies was cooked in earlier stars.

chapters.title: Mapping the Universe
chapters.tease: Counting galaxies in 3D turned cosmology into a precision science and found the cosmic web's walls and voids.

chapters.title: The Cosmic Calendar
chapters.tease: Squeezing 13.8 billion years into one year makes deep time something a human mind can feel.

chapters.title: How It All Ends
chapters.tease: The fate of everything depends on dark energy, and new surveys are finally measuring it well enough to tell.

chapters.title: Worlds Beyond
chapters.tease: It turned other worlds from philosophy into a census: planets are the rule, not the exception.

chapters.title: The Transit Method
chapters.tease: It turned faint dips in starlight into thousands of planets, with their sizes, years and even their air.

chapters.title: The Wobble Method
chapters.tease: It weighed the first planet around a Sun-like star, and still gives the masses of most nearby worlds.

chapters.title: Hot Jupiters
chapters.tease: They proved giant planets wander, overturning a theory of planet formation built on our solar system alone.

chapters.title: Super-Earths & Mini-Neptunes
chapters.tease: The galaxy's most common planets are a type our solar system lacks, so studying them redraws what normal means.

chapters.title: The Habitable Zone
chapters.tease: It tells telescopes where to look first for life, and reminds us how narrow Earth's own margins are.

chapters.title: TRAPPIST-1
chapters.tease: Seven Earth-sized worlds around one nearby star made it the best lab for asking whether red dwarfs host life.

chapters.title: Biosignatures
chapters.tease: It makes the question of whether anyone is out there a measurable one: chemistry read from starlight.

chapters.title: The Drake Equation
chapters.tease: It turned the question of whether we are alone into a set of measurable steps, and showed where our ignorance lies.

chapters.title: SETI
chapters.tease: It is humanity's attempt to answer the oldest question by experiment: is anyone else out there transmitting?

chapters.title: How Telescopes Work
chapters.tease: Two ways to tame light, bending and bouncing, turned vague glimmers into measurable worlds.

chapters.title: Light Buckets
chapters.tease: Each doubling of mirror size quadrupled the light caught, and opened a new, fainter layer of the universe.

chapters.title: Radio Astronomy
chapters.tease: Radio revealed pulsars, quasars and cold hydrogen, then linked dishes into a planet-sized eye.

chapters.title: Hubble Space Telescope
chapters.tease: Rescued in orbit, Hubble became the sharpest eye on the sky and the face of modern astronomy.

chapters.title: James Webb Space Telescope
chapters.tease: Webb sees the first galaxies and the air of distant worlds, from a cold perch 1.5 million km away.

chapters.title: Spectroscopy
chapters.tease: Splitting light into its colours let astronomers read what stars are made of, from light-years away.

chapters.title: Adaptive Optics
chapters.tease: It cancels the atmosphere's blur in real time, giving giant ground telescopes space-sharp eyes.

chapters.title: Hearing Spacetime
chapters.tease: Gravitational-wave detectors gave astronomy a new sense: feeling spacetime itself ripple.

chapters.title: Vera Rubin Observatory
chapters.tease: Rubin turns the night sky from a photograph into a ten-year film, catching everything that changes.

chapters.title: Observatories of Tomorrow
chapters.tease: Telescopes now being built may answer whether a nearby planet has the atmosphere of a living world.

chapters.title: The Rocket Equation
chapters.tease: One line of 1903 maths decides how big every rocket must be, and why reaching orbit is so hard.

chapters.title: Sputnik to Apollo
chapters.tease: A superpower rivalry turned a beeping ball into twelve moonwalkers in fifteen years.

chapters.title: Robotic Pioneers
chapters.tease: Robots reached every planet first, turning points of light into mapped worlds we know by name.

chapters.title: The Voyagers
chapters.tease: Two 1970s probes toured the giant planets and are now the only working craft in interstellar space.

chapters.title: Mars Rovers
chapters.tease: Thirty years of patient robot geologists showed that Mars was once wet enough to host life.

chapters.title: The ISS
chapters.tease: Five agencies built a home in orbit, and humans have lived off the planet without a break since 2000.

chapters.title: Sample Returns
chapters.tease: Bringing other worlds into Earth's labs lets the best instruments ever built ask questions for decades.

chapters.title: Return to the Moon
chapters.tease: Half a century after Apollo, people are heading back to the Moon, this time to its icy south pole, to stay.

chapters.title: The Commercial Space Age
chapters.tease: Rockets that land and fly again made space routine, and filled the sky with thousands of satellites.

chapters.title: Where Next?
chapters.tease: The next frontiers are a Moon base, footprints on Mars and robot divers in alien oceans.

chapters.title: Multi-Messenger Astronomy
chapters.tease: Light was astronomy's only messenger for millennia. Now spacetime ripples and ghost particles carry news too.

chapters.title: The Kilonova Moment
chapters.tease: Two dead stars collided, and the world heard it, saw it and found gold being forged in the wreckage.

chapters.title: Hunting Dark Matter
chapters.tease: Five-sixths of all matter is invisible. The most sensitive detectors ever built are still waiting for their first touch.

chapters.title: The Hubble Tension
chapters.tease: Two careful ways of timing cosmic expansion disagree by 9 per cent. Either one is wrong, or physics is incomplete.

chapters.title: JWST's Impossible Galaxies
chapters.tease: Webb found galaxies that grew up too fast, forcing a rewrite of the universe's first chapter.

chapters.title: The Sky as a Movie
chapters.tease: Rubin films the whole southern sky every few nights and tells the world within a minute when something changes.

chapters.title: Interstellar Visitors
chapters.tease: Three objects born around other stars have crossed our solar system since 2017, each a sample from another world.

chapters.title: The Biggest Questions
chapters.tease: We cannot yet name 95 per cent of the universe, but we can now say exactly which experiments might.

chapters.title: Everyone's Sky
chapters.tease: Back-garden observers and online volunteers still discover comets, supernovae and strange new objects.

chapters.title: We Are Star-Stuff
chapters.tease: Every atom in you was made in the Big Bang or inside stars. Astronomy is the universe studying its own history.
